one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-11-20 to 2026-12-20: no earnings (Q1 FY27 report expected mid/late Feb 2027). Events: CFO handover to Jason Kary (December, announced on the call), the mid-December FOMC meeting, and post-print estimate revisions. Short-horizon regularities favor mild upside: post-earnings drift after a beat-and-raise with the Q1 guide ~4% above revenue consensus and ~14% above EPS consensus, and reversal after the -7.1% Nov 20 close (Nov 23 trades near 290 intraday on thin early volume). I center the distribution at ~272 (+4% vs 261.51, a partial credit to the rebound and drift) with a monthly sigma of 0.14 (48% annual vol / 3.5), no skew view.

fair_value.method: Quarterly driver build (FY27-29 revenue 8,523 / 9,680 / 10,766; segment non-GAAP margins from the clean Q4 FY26 exit stepping to mid-cycle) valued with NTM P/E 18.5x on ~$17.2 EPS (0.45), FCF yield 4.75% (0.30) and mid-cycle-margin earnings x 18.5x (0.25): $307.41.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (FY28-weighted) non-GAAP EPS ~$17.2 at the horizon x 18.5x (peer median 18.75x at 2026-11-20 prices; KEYS 19.0x; k = 0.8; -0.45 turn post-horizon risk)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 quarters 358/428/520/635 = CC less the wireless estimate (Q4 635 is +105% on the Q4 FY25 estimate 310, consistent with the CFO's 'triple-digit'). Forecast FY growth = 1/3 x optics market growth (manufacturing test scales with transceiver units) + 2/3 x R&D test growth (wireline ~two-thirds R&D, Q3 FY26 call): FY27 1/3 x 76% + 2/3 x 25% = 42.0% -> 2756; FY28 1/3 x 62% + 2/3 x 12% = 28.7% -> 3546; FY29 1/3 x 48% + 2/3 x 8% = 21.3% -> 4303. Market 2028-29 is a straight-line interpolation of LightCounting's 76% (2027) to 20% (2031) path (estimate). R&D growth +25/12/8% is the main judgment: below the market because R&D test buys precede volume and fade as 1.6T matures; record backlog supports FY27. Quarters: one constant sequential growth rate per year from the prior Q4 (capacity-paced shipments under the supply constraint the CEO described), not a past seasonal shape. Alternatives: (a) R&D +15/10/5% gives FY27 2627; (b) wireline grows with the market (+76/62/48%); (c) LightCounting 'Bumpy Ride' correction in 2028 (downside case).
inputs_detail.variant_view: If wireline tracks the optics market one-for-one FY27 revenue rises ~+$0.9B; a 2028 correction (Bumpy Ride) cuts FY28 wireline by a third.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 1,826 (400/430/486/510; Spirent in all FY26 quarters). FY27 2066 (+13.1%): the Q4 exit rate 510 x 4 = 2,040 plus modest sequential growth (+0.5%/qtr) as double-digit order growth converts; FY28 +6% and FY29 +5% as 6G R&D builds toward standardisation (CEO: early 6G development). Alternatives: FY24-type wireless decline (-7%); order growth converting in full (+12%).
inputs_detail.variant_view: A handset/RAN capex pause as in FY24 (-7%) would cut FY27 by ~$0.4B vs base.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 +8% -> 1543: strong double-digit Q4 orders against +7% Q4 revenue; FY26's +15% included acquisitions; FY28 +6%, FY29 +5%. Alternative: a continuing-resolution budget year holds growth near +3%. Defense exposure flagged (rule 0: KEYS is not a defense name; ADG is 20% of revenue).

FY27 +10% -> 2157 (orders up six quarters; AI semis, PCB interconnect, automotive software-defined vehicles), FY28 +7%, FY29 +6% as the industrial cycle matures. Alternative: an FY24-type industrial/auto downturn (-12%), weighted through the Kalshi 2027 recession market (20%).

FY26 CSG 33.4% (1,733/5,196), 32.6% before the Q2 IEEPA refund (+$38M). FY27 36.6% (quarters 36.5/36.5/36.5/37.0): the Q4 FY26 exit 37.1% had no IEEPA refund, so it is the clean run rate; we take 0.6pt off it because the CFO guides gross margin only 'stable' (no further mix gain) while opex steps up with the capacity build, then +0.5pt in Q4 (Q4 margin above Q3 in FY25 and FY26 releases). KEYS shows no Q1 margin dip (Q1 FY26 27.4% vs Q4 FY25 26.3%). Cross-check: the Q1 EPS guide 3.63-3.69 implies ~35.6% company margin. FY28 36.1% (-0.5pt: pricing normalises as 1.6T test matures), FY29 35.1% (-1pt toward mid-cycle; playbook: the third year is not a peak; KEYS company non-GAAP operating margin ran ~24-30% over FY23-FY25). Alternatives: FY26 ex-refund 32.6% held; Q4 exit 37.1% held.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Mix normalising to FY26 ex-refund 32.6% cuts FY27 EPS by ~$1.3.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM levered FCF per share at the horizon / 4.75% (peer median TTM 3.2% x 1.184 growth = 3.79% NTM; KEYS 5.0%; k = 0.8)

inputs_detail.derivation: Adjusted EBIT excludes acquisition amortization, so only depreciation is added back: FY26 depreciation 153 / 7,157 = 2.14%; rising 0.1pt a year as the ~$275M capex step (2x FY26) depreciates.
FY27 3.3% x 8,523 = 281 vs CFO ~275 (guide use declared in guidance_check); FY28-29 fall as the capacity step completes and revenue grows (FY23-FY26 ratio 3.6% / 3.1% / 2.4% / 1.9%).

anchor.note: FY26 capex 139 / 7,157 = 1.94%; the gap is the announced FY27 capacity step (CFO ~$275M).

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26: non-GAAP net income ~2,030 (11.72 x 173) + depreciation 153 - capex 139 - FCF 1,747 = 297 absorbed by working capital and other on a revenue increase of 1,782 -> 16.7%.

Peer median TTM levered FCF yield 3.2% (secfacts); put on an NTM basis x (1 + peer median forward EPS growth 18.4%) = 3.79%; KEYS own NTM 5.0% (FY27 build FCF ~2,220 / market cap 44,510); k = 0.8 -> 3.79 x (5.0/3.79)^0.8 = 4.73%, rounded 4.75%. No SBC deduction (rule).
inputs_detail.variant_view: On TTM basis (peer 3.2%, own 3.9%, k -> 3.75%) the leg is ~$85/share higher; we reject the basis mix.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Mid-cycle: NTM revenue 9,680 x 25.17% mid-cycle non-GAAP net margin (FY23-26 average) / 170.9M shares = $14.26 x 18.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: Base-rate normalised-earnings leg (playbook cross-check, weight 0.25, judgment, untested; not driver-linked: a stated per-share value that scenarios move by custom_pct). Mid-cycle non-GAAP net margin = average of FY23-FY26 non-GAAP EPS x diluted shares / revenue: FY23 8.33 x 179 / 5,464 = 27.3%; FY24 6.27 x 175 / 4,979 = 22.0%; FY25 7.15 (= FY26 11.72 / 1.64, 'up 64%') x 173 / 5,375 = 23.0%; FY26 11.72 x 173 / 7,157 = 28.3%; mean 25.17% (one full up-down-up cycle). x NTM revenue at the horizon 9,680 (driver build) / 170.9M horizon shares = $14.26; x the same 18.5x exit P/E = $263.7. It prices the stock as if FY28 margins sat at the cycle average rather than the build's ~34%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At FY26 margins (28.3%) the leg would be ~$300.

downside.story: 10th percentile: LightCounting's 'Bumpy Ride' case arrives in 2027-28: hyperscaler 800G/1.6T capacity lands and R&D test budgets pause, so wireline runs 45% below the build (FY28 ~1,950 vs 3,546, about the FY26 level); wireless -8% (an FY24-type RAN/handset pause), EISG -12% (an FY24-type industrial downturn; Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20%), segment margins -5pt toward FY25 levels, and the P/E derates 5 turns to ~13.5x as the market prices a cyclical peak (the Oct-2023 trough was 14.6x trailing non-GAAP EPS: 122.05 / 8.33). Like Dec-2021 to Oct-2023 (-42.6% over 22 months, Trefis).

base.story: Median: FY27 revenue 8,523 (+19.1%, a touch below the CEO's +20% base case), FY28 9,680 (+13.6%), FY29 10,766; CSG margin 36.6% / 36.1% / 35.1%, EISG 31.4% / 31.0% / 30.0%; NTM EPS at the horizon ~$17.2 x 18.5x, the FCF-yield leg at 4.75% and a mid-cycle-margin leg (25.2% net) at 25% weight.

upside.story: 90th percentile: wireline tracks the optics market rather than R&D budgets (LightCounting +76% 2027 holds and 3.2T / co-packaged-optics R&D starts), +28% vs the build; supply eases so the record backlog converts, EISG +6%, margins +2pt, and the P/E re-rates 5 turns to ~23.5x as AI test is treated as structural.

reasoning: Base-rate lane first. KEYS's own 12-month returns since mid-2019 (Twelve Data monthly closes, 78 windows) run P10 -14%, median +12%, P90 +89%; after the five months that sat 20%+ below a recent high the next 12 months returned +2% to +22%. Trefis (2026-11-03) counts five 20%+ drawdowns since 2016; four recovered within 2-8 months, the exception being Dec-2021 to Oct-2023 (-42.6%, 26 months to recover) - the template for the downside case, which also uses Kalshi's 20% 2027 recession price (volume 18K/day, OI 454K, 2026-11-22). The current setup is a beat-and-raise met by selling: Q4 FY26 revenue 1,994 vs guide 1,930-1,950, EPS 3.61 vs 3.34-3.40, orders 2,339 (book-to-bill 1.17), Q1 guide 2.04-2.06B / 3.63-3.69 vs pre-print consensus 1.96B / 3.21, CEO base case +20% for FY27 - yet the stock closed -7.1% on Nov 20 (281.42 -> 261.51) and is down from 389.93; Nov 23 trades ~290. The base rate after such resets is recovery, not further collapse, unless the AI optics cycle turns. Model: rebased on FY26 actuals (7,157). Wireline (not disclosed; ~1,941 in FY26 from CC less wireless) grows at 1/3 x LightCounting's optics market growth (+76% 2027, interpolated +62%/+48%) + 2/3 x R&D test growth (+25/12/8%, judgment): +42%/+29%/+21%. Wireless +13% FY27 (exit run rate, double-digit orders), ADG +8%, EI +10%, then fading. Margins start from the clean Q4 exit (no IEEPA refund) and step down toward mid-cycle by FY29. FY27 revenue 8,523 sits +4.6% above the stale pre-print consensus and 0.7% below the CEO's +20%; our Q1 EPS 3.58 is just below the guide low because we do not book margin expansion beyond the Q4 exit. Valuation: P/E 18.5x (peer median 18.75x at Nov-20 prices, KEYS 19.0x, k = 0.8, -0.45 turn post-horizon risk) on NTM EPS ~$17.2 gives $318; FCF yield 4.75% (NTM basis) gives $329; mid-cycle margin x the same P/E gives $264 (not driver-linked). Blend $307 (+17.6% vs $261.51). Scenarios are driver moves sized from the record: P10 $201 (-23%) replays 2022-23 with an optics correction; P90 $402 (+54%) needs wireline to track the optics market and a re-rating. Research was limited for post-print consensus and analyst notes (blocked or stale pages, listed in gap_note).
